crate.name: A drift crate
lines: A tea crate, stencilled HEARTHBAY PACKET. The tea went to the fish long ago.
A fish box with a rope handle. Somebody packed it carefully, and then the sea did.
A crate of lamp-oil tins, all empty but one, and that one full of coins.
A bait box with a brass catch. The catch is warm.
A crate addressed to the lighthouse, in ink that has not run. Nobody has written to the lighthouse in years.

chest.name: A sea chest
lines: A sea chest off the Teeth, bound in iron the rust has not found.
A chest with a rope becket, and initials burned out of the lid with a poker.
A chest packed for a long voyage: oilskins, a tin plate, a pearl in a twist of paper. The label says only BACK SOON.

crate.name: A fen crate
lines: A survey crate, lettered I.C. in a hand that is not Dr. Calloway's.
A reed-cutter's box, green right through. The moss has kept it shut.
A crate off the packet with the label still dry. It is addressed to Sedge Landing, and to nobody.
A tin trunk with a lily growing out of the lock.
A crate of preserving jars, every one of them empty, every lid waxed down.

chest.name: A sea chest
lines: A chest gone green, the hinges sweet. It was fastened from the inside.
A chest roped round twice, with every knot on the underside.
A chest that came up lighter than it went down. Whatever was let out of it left a pearl behind, for manners.
